tools.description: Runs actions in order in the session, until one fails: input, captures, windows, processes, clipboard. Captures are returned as images. Each step is an object with the action's name in "action" and only the properties its schema lists, e.g. {"action": "Mouse.Click", "x": 640, "y": 360}, {"action": "Keyboard.Type", "text": "hello"}, {"action": "Keyboard.Tap", "key": "S", "modifiers": ["Ctrl"]}, {"action": "Control.Wait", "duration": 500}, {"action": "Capture.Window", "title": "Notepad"}. Invalid steps are all reported at once, and then nothing runs. AI clients often give up on a tool call after about a minute, so keep each sequence's waits well below that; for longer work, start it in the background (Process.Run with async) and check on it with short sequences. A sequence the client gives up on is stopped. When the user locks the PC, input actions wait the few seconds SecondShell takes to keep input working; they fail with InputUnavailable when input does not come back soon (the message, and Check-Session, tell why). The response also tells what changed since your previous call (events, newWindows).

anyOf.description: Runs a command in the session. Synchronous by default: waits for the exit and returns the exit code and the output and error streams (each truncated to 64 KB). Use async for programs that keep running, e.g. GUI applications or a console to interact with: it starts the program as Explorer would and returns its process ID at once; with shell None the ID is the program's own. Start a packaged (Store) app through its execution alias with workingDirectory set to its package folder, as some load files relative to it.

args.description: Arguments of the program in command, each passed as it is, never parsed by the shell, e.g. ["/c", "dir"] with command "cmd.exe".

async.description: Start the program as Explorer would (console programs get a window, nothing is redirected) and return its process ID at once; Control.Join does not wait for it, Process.WaitForProcess does.

command.description: Without args: a command line for the shell, e.g. "Get-ChildItem C:\\Temp | Select-Object -First 5". With args, or with shell None: the program to run, e.g. "cmd.exe" or "C:\\Tools\\tool.exe" (in PowerShell also a script or cmdlet).

shell.description: PowerShell (Windows PowerShell), Pwsh (PowerShell 7), Cmd, or None (no shell: command is an executable); default: the user's setting, PowerShell unless they changed it.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the exit, default 10000; when it expires the sequence stops with a Timeout error and the process keeps running.

anyOf.description: Asks a process to exit gracefully: its windows get a close request, console processes get Ctrl+C. Returns its exit code; use Process.Kill if it does not exit.

pid.description: The process ID, e.g. from Process.Run or Process.Enumerate.
